summary.text: This briefing explores combining global local attention, transformer, and decoder techniques to address feature misalignment and high computational costs in tasks like audio-visual speech separation and infrared small target detection. Integrating global-local attention blocks within a transformer-based encoder-decoder or dual-path architecture enables efficient capture of multi-scale dependencies alongside fine-grained spatial features. Evidence suggests that such combined structures can successfully handle complex spatial details and semantic contexts.

jtbd.text: When processing high-resolution spatial details and long-range semantic contexts for target extraction tasks, developers want to efficiently capture multi-scale dependencies without incurring high computational costs, so that they can resolve feature misalignment in complex environments.

value_prop.text: Combining global local attention with transformer and decoder components helps reconcile the conflict between capturing high-resolution spatial details for small targets and extracting robust semantic context for larger structures. This integration aims to improve operational efficiency and multi-scale feature alignment in target processing tasks.

riskiest_assumption.text: The feasibility score of 2.0 indicates that integrating global local attention with transformer decoders may suffer from severe architectural incompatibility or prohibitive computational bottlenecks during multi-scale feature fusion, potentially preventing stable on-device execution.

mvp.text: As a technical proof of concept from existing packages, build a minimal script using Hugging Face transformers and deepspeed to construct a small encoder-decoder model featuring global local attention blocks. Run a baseline inference test on sample audio or visual data to measure processing latency and memory usage against a proposed threshold of less than 200 milliseconds per batch.
mvp.type: technical proof of concept from existing packages

success_metric.text: The MVP successfully demonstrates feasibility if the prototype achieves a processing latency reduction of a proposed threshold: 30 percent compared to standard full-attention baselines while maintaining token alignment accuracy above a proposed threshold: 85 percent.

kill_criteria.text: The MVP is abandoned if the integration of global local attention into the decoder architecture causes gradient explosion or complete training divergence, failing to converge within a proposed threshold of 10 epochs.
The concept is killed if the inference memory consumption exceeds a proposed threshold of 4 GB on standard hardware, negating the expected efficiency gains.

open_source.use: Provides foundational transformer model definitions and utilities to construct the encoder-decoder architecture.
Enables optimized distributed training and mixed-precision execution to manage memory overhead during multi-scale attention experiments.

to_build.text: A custom global-local attention block layer designed to interface directly with the decoder hidden states for multi-scale feature fusion.
